title: Ren'Py translation game profile
description: Per-game/per-language config consumed by extract_strings.py, translate_api.py, qa_check.py, and build_patch.py. All relative paths are resolved against the profile file's directory.

game_name.description: Display name of the game, e.g. "Being a DIK"

language_id.description: Ren'Py language key; also the patch folder name game/tl/<language_id>/. Lowercase, no spaces, e.g. "thai", "french"

progress_file.description: Translations JSON: {english: translation}. Written incrementally; resumable.

speakers.description: Speaker code (as it appears in the .rpy scripts) -> character record. This IS the character dictionary: it feeds the persona card in the translation prompt, the register rules in qa_check.py, and TM context. Only `name` is required — a record with just name/gender/role behaves exactly as it did before v1.4.

role.description: One-line description: relationship to protagonist, personality, register hints

alias_of.description: This code is the same person as another code — common in visual novels where a character is '???' until introduced. Everything else in this record is ignored; the target's record is used, and the two codes share QA rules.

called.description: Names and nicknames the script uses to ADDRESS this character ("Mr. Reed", "Sis"). Feeds the vocative tier of addressee resolution; the record's `name` is included automatically. Add the forms that actually appear in dialog, not every possible variant.

register.description: Prose voice guidance: formality, warmth, sentence rhythm, slang tolerance.

self_pronoun.description: Default first-person pronoun/speech level. Override per relationship in `to`.

address_pronoun.description: Default second-person pronoun. Override per relationship in `to`.

forbidden.description: Terms this character must NEVER use, in any context. Shown in the prompt AND enforced as a category-2 QA rule, so the gate checks what the prompt asked for.

must_use.description: Vocabulary that should appear in this character's longer lines (verbal tics, signature terms). Advisory — reported as a phrasing flag, never a hard failure.

speech_notes.description: Hard rules and exceptions that don't fit the other fields.

monologue.description: Overrides for inner-thought lines wrapped in (...) — a character often addresses themselves differently than anyone else.

to.description: Per-relationship overrides, keyed by the OTHER speaker's code. In register-rich languages the pronoun is a property of the pair, not the person: the same protagonist may use a casual pronoun with a close friend and a formal one with an authority figure. Always shown to the translator as a table; from v1.5 the row that applies to a line is also named outright wherever the addressee could be resolved confidently (see `relationships`).

forbidden.description: Terms this character must never use TO this particular person (crude pronouns toward a professor, a nickname only one friend is allowed). Enforced as a category-3 QA rule, but only on lines whose addressee resolved at or above min_confidence — an unresolved line is never judged against a relationship.

examples.description: Approved EN -> target renderings for this character. Two are shown per prompt; a `note` explaining WHY the rendering is right is worth more than a third example.

relationships.description: Addressee resolution: which character each line is spoken TO, so the right row of `speakers[x].to` can be applied. Answers come from named evidence only and every line the evidence does not cover stays unresolved. Omit entirely for the defaults.

enabled.description: Defaults to true when the profile declares any relationship data (a `to` map on some character, or a `declared` scope), false otherwise — so a profile that never mentions relationships behaves exactly as it did before v1.5.

min_confidence.description: The weakest evidence tier allowed to drive prompts, TM context, and QA rules. `declared` = a scope below names the pair; `vocative` = the English line addresses someone by name in vocative position; `dyad` = the enclosing Ren'Py label has exactly two character speakers. Raising this withholds weaker answers; they still appear in the relationships.py report.

declared.description: Hand-authored addressee scopes, checked in order; the first match wins and outranks every other tier. Use them for the passages resolution gets wrong or cannot see — a crowded scene, a phone call, a letter read aloud.

items.description: Constrain with any of file/label/lines, then name the pairing with `pairs` or `cast`.

file.description: Restrict to one .rpy file (basename, as it appears in strings.json).

pairs.description: Speaker code -> addressee code. Only the speakers listed resolve.

cast.description: Shorthand for a two-person exchange: each of the two addresses the other.

keep_untranslated.description: Names and proper nouns that must stay exactly as written (no translation/transliteration). Also whitelists them for qa_check's untranslated-roman-word check.

style_guide_file.description: Markdown style guide (registers, formality, slang policy, few-shot examples). Loaded into the system prompt by translate_api.py, and into context by whichever assistant translates in-session.

qa_rules_file.description: Declarative register/phrasing rules for qa_check.py. See references/qa.md.

font.description: Omit entirely if the game's fonts already cover the target script.

regular.description: Target-script font filename (must be copied into game/)

replace_fonts.description: The game's original font files to substitute via config.font_replacement_map

size_scale.description: Multiplier applied to base_sizes when the target language is active (some fonts render smaller at the same point size)

base_sizes.description: Style name -> the game's original point size for that style

styles.description: Style names to override; defaults to the common Ren'Py text styles

toggle_key.description: pygame key constant for the in-game language toggle

auto_set_language.description: Switch the game to the target language automatically on first launch (useful when the game has no language picker in Preferences)

tm.description: Translation Memory: a durable source->translation cache consulted by translate_api.py before calling the LLM, and the CLI translation_memory.py. Managed only via the TranslationMemory class, never edited by hand.

enabled.description: Set false to bypass the TM entirely (every string goes to the LLM).

path.description: TM JSON location; relative paths resolve against the profile directory. Default: .ftp/translation_memory.json (project-local). Point at a shared/global file to reuse translations across games (cost win, but a register risk for character dialog).

validation.description: Output validity gates shared by translate_api.py (which refuses to save or cache a failing translation) and qa_check.py (which reports the same failures as category 1). Omit entirely for the defaults.

echo_check.description: Reject a translation identical to its source. Language-neutral and safe to leave on: sources whose only translatable content is a keep_untranslated term, a variable, a tag, or punctuation are exempt automatically.

script_check.description: Reject a translation containing no target-script characters. Effective ONLY when target_script is set explicitly — inferring it from language_id would turn on a new hard failure for existing profiles on upgrade.

target_script.description: A named script (thai, lao, khmer, japanese, chinese, korean, cyrillic, greek, arabic, hebrew, devanagari, ...) or explicit codepoint ranges: {"ranges": ["0E00-0E7F"]}. Setting this is what enables script_check. Latin-script targets cannot be checked this way (they share codepoints with the source).

allow_identical.description: Exact source strings permitted to pass through unchanged (e.g. a line that is genuinely the same in both languages). Hand-maintained; nothing populates it automatically. Use it for the residue the keep_untranslated exemption doesn't cover.

min_script_chars.description: Target-script characters a translation must contain to pass script_check.

provider.description: deepseek is a preset for DeepSeek's official API (base_url, key env, model, and thinking mode pre-set). openai-compatible speaks the same OpenAI Chat Completions wire format for any other endpoint — OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, Azure — selected via base_url. claude-cli drives a locally installed Claude Code CLI headlessly (no API key).

model.description: Defaults per provider: gemini → gemini-2.5-pro, anthropic → claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-cli → sonnet, openai-compatible → gpt-4o-mini, deepseek → deepseek-v4-flash (use deepseek-v4-pro for a harder pass). The legacy aliases deepseek-chat / deepseek-reasoner were retired 2026-07-24; they are still sent if you set them, with a warning.

thinking.description: deepseek only. DeepSeek V4 enables thinking mode by default; this preset turns it OFF because reasoning tokens count against max_tokens (a long chain of thought can consume the whole budget and return an EMPTY answer) and because thinking mode rejects temperature, silently discarding the low value this pipeline uses for consistency. Batch translation is not a reasoning task. Set true for a quality-critical pass.

reasoning_effort.description: deepseek only, and only when thinking is true. deepseek-v4-flash supports all three; deepseek-v4-pro supports high and max.

escalate_max_tokens.description: When a reply comes back empty because it hit max_tokens, retry that call once with a 4x budget and keep the raised value for the rest of the run (so discovery is paid once, not per batch). Capped at 65536. Set false to fail immediately instead.

base_url.description: openai-compatible only. /chat/completions is appended. DeepSeek: https://api.deepseek.com/v1 · OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 · Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1 · Azure: https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/<deployment>

api_key_env.description: openai-compatible only. Name of the environment variable (or .env entry) holding the key. A localhost base_url needs no key.

api_key_header.description: openai-compatible only. Authorization sends 'Bearer <key>'; set to api-key for Azure, which sends the raw key.

max_tokens.description: Response ceiling for the anthropic and openai-compatible providers.

json_mode.description: openai-compatible only. Sends response_format={"type":"json_object"}. Off by default because support varies across OpenAI-compatible backends; the prompt already specifies the output contract, and object-wrapped replies are unwrapped either way.
